newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourses fall sharply, hit by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourses fall sharply, hit by Wall St.

text.p: European bourses fell sharply on Monday, rattled by a weak opening on Wall Street where jitters over higher interest rates took hold.

On Currency markets, the dollar lost a pfennig as traders fretted over a batch of German figures this week, which could signal returning strength to the German economy, good news for the mark against the dollar.
The dull performance in European stocks was in stark contrast to a strong showing last Friday which saw London, Frankfurt and Paris end with big gains as Wall Street climbed.
In London, stocks slipped by over one percent, pushed down by Wall Street's weak opening rather than political concerns over the announcement of Britain's general election date, May 1.

Prime Minister John Major ended months of speculation by setting the date but the news failed to set pulses racing in the stock market -- analysts said the election date, and an expected victory for the opposition Labour Party, were already discounted.

The London markets was depressed by the dilution of stocks with several big companies going ex-dividend as well as Wall Street, pulled down by weakness in bonds on anticipation of an interest rate hike when the U.S. central bank's policy-making Federal Open Markets Committee (FOMC) meets on March 25. "I think the market is doing some anticipatory selling ahead of the March 25 FOMC meeting on nervousness that rates will be increased," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
Joe Rooney, strategist at Lehman Brothers, said the election announcement would have little impact despite the likely win for Labour, traditionally regarded as less friendly to business.
"The election announcement hasn't done anything to the market, we all knew it was coming," one dealer said. "Half the fall is from ex-dividends and the rest is worries about Wall Street."

In Frankfurt, floor trade, which ended before New York opened, lost early gains to close with a modest 0.25 percent loss. The computerised IBIS index was down by nearly two percent in the early afternoon.
Dealers blamed the falling dollar which dimmed export prospects, adding that speculation about the start of Europe's monetary union added a degree of confusion to a market.
"Markets around Europe are a bit drifty but we don't see any real selling (in the German market)," one trader said.

Speculation had been fuelled about a possible delay to the launch of EMU by an article in the Bild newspaper quoting German finance minister Theo Waigel as saying that adherence to the EMU criteria was more important than to the timetable.
Paris was hit badly by the downturn in sentiment, also dropping nearly two percent by mid-afternoon.
Traders said investors were worried about the weak dollar and volatility of the markets. Trade was likely to be cautious before U.S. housing starts data on Tuesday and inflation figures on Wednesday.
On currency markets, the dollar fell sharply against the mark but recovered most early losses against the yen. Trade was thin.

"Dollar/mark is going through a bit of a clear-out at the moment, there's no news driving it and people are generally still looking for a firmer dollar in the medium-term," said a Japanese bank dealer.
Many traders were awaiting word on American interest rates which could come from the next FOMC session. Opinion is divided over what action the Fed will take.
The main focus for later this week was on German economic data which includes the February IFO business climate survey, February M3 money supply and German price data.
The data will be eyed closely for any sign of returning strength to the German economy which will be mark supportive.
"There is little on the news front and the moves at the moment are really consolidative," said a UK bank dealer. "The focus is on the German data and U.S. trade numbers this week."
Sterling recovered some ground after Major called the election for May 1, but later sank again to test fresh six-week lows of 2.6795 marks.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6891 marks and 123.70 yen, compared with Friday's late European levels of 1.6972 marks and 123.45 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 42.9 points at 4,381.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 51.09 points at 2,595.19.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down down 8.3 points at 3,350.99.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $351.40 compared with $352.75 at the close on Friday. Silver was at $5.23, compared with $5.31 on Friday.
